description:
## Contract risk

calendars-client `calendar_event_query` takes:

```rust
sort: Option<&[CalendarEventComparator]>,
```

at crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/event.rs:155.

Canonical mail-client `email_query` takes:

```rust
sort: Option<serde_json::Value>,
```

at crate-jmap-mail-client/src/methods/email.rs:144.

JMAP-1j9k.2 already names the lockout angle for the `filter` param. This bead
covers the same angle for the `sort` param, which the existing finding does
not call out explicitly. The two divergences are linked: both pin the wire
shape to a specific Rust type owned by jmap-calendars-types.

## Why this matters for a caller

A caller who wants to sort by a comparator type the spec adds in a future
draft revision is locked out until jmap-calendars-types catches up and a new
calendars-client release ships. With the untyped canonical shape, a caller can
construct any spec-defined comparator JSON inline:

```rust
let sort = json!([{"property": "newProperty", "isAscending": false}]);
sc.email_query(filter, Some(sort), None, None, None).await?;
```

The typed `&[CalendarEventComparator]` shape requires the calendars-types
crate to ship a Rust variant for every comparator the spec defines. Until
then, the caller's only path is to fork.

Also note `calendar_event_notification_query` is asymmetric: filter is typed
(`Option<&NotificationFilterCondition>` at event_notification.rs:138) but sort
is `Option<&[serde_json::Value]>` at event_notification.rs:139. The doc
comment at event_notification.rs:132-135 explicitly explains: 'CalendarEventNotification's
Comparator type in jmap-calendars-types is serde_json::Value because the
spec's sort properties for notifications are minimal (just `created`); the
slice is forwarded as-is.' That rationale applies equally to the regular
`calendar_event_query` sort — the typed wrapping is doing no work the caller
can use.

## What goes wrong if this stays

Same lock-in mechanism as JMAP-1j9k.2 — once shipped in 0.x.y, the typed
shapes are public API; relaxing them to untyped JSON is a breaking change.

## Fix shape

Match the canonical: `Option<serde_json::Value>` for both filter and sort.
Or, define a single `_query` params struct (one positional arg, like
`MailboxSetParams`) that accepts the typed types where useful AND lets
callers escape-hatch to a raw `serde_json::Value` for the untyped path.

title: calendar_event_query and calendar_event_notification_query sort param locks out untyped JSON (complementary to JMAP-1j9k.2)
